To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a novel recurrent spatial transformer network (RNN-SPN) model, (2) we show that the RPN-SPN model can down-sample the input image without deteriorating performance, and (3) we show that our model achieves superior classification performance on the cluttered MNIST dataset

(1) the proposed recurrent spatial transformer networks can learn adaptive down-sampling, which minimizes the information lost in the regions of interests, (2) the proposed recurrent SPNs can outperform state-of-the-art models on the MNIST sequence dataset, (3) the proposed recurrent transformer network is able to learn to downsample the input images without any explicit training signal, which is an important property for future research on learning to zoom

we propose a recurrent neural network that integrates the spatial transformer network into a recurrent neural architecture and we show how this recurrent network outperforms a convolutional network and convolutional networks with spatial transformer layers on a sequence classification task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following contributions.
recurrent networks that learn to attend to regions of interests in a sequence of images.
recurrent neural networks that are able to zoom, rotate, and skew their input.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNN-SPNs outperform convolutional networks with and without SPN layers in digit recognition in MNIST and MNIST sequences.
RNN-SPNs are a powerful tool for image classification and can outperform other methods.
we show how to combine a spatial transformer network with recurrent neural networks and show that it improves the performance on the MNIST dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
recurrent networks with spatial transformer layers are better than convolutional networks with or without spatial transformer layers.
the proposed RNN-SPNs are able to adaptively down-sample the input sequences to focus on regions of interest and thus perform better than other methods.
we show that recurrent networks can be combined with spatial transformers to form a powerful sequence model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNNs are a natural fit for SPNs and that the RNNs can learn to attend to the regions of interest in a sequence of images.
the SPN is a powerful tool for RNNs and we believe that it will be useful in a variety of RNN-based applications.
the SPN is not only useful for classification, but can also be integrated in RNNs to perform sequence modeling tasks.
